typography.$description:
Real-usage audit (2026-07-23) found a genuine gap this scale doesn't cover: 13px recurs heavily across 3 of the 5 apps (career-web, client-web, recruitment-portal — 116+ combined instances) sitting right between paragraph-xsmall (12px) and paragraph-small (14px). RESOLUTION (2026-07-25): not formalized as its own token — 13px is almost certainly Figma/rem-rounding drift (0.8125rem is an unusually precise, non-round rem value for a deliberate design choice) rather than an intentional size. Recommended fix at the code level: snap any text-[13px] usage to paragraph-small (14px), the single most dominant body size in every app, rather than inventing a permanent token to match an accident. Typography is also now emitted as composite Tailwind component classes (e.g. .text-h2 bundling size+line-height+weight+tracking in one class) rather than relying on separately-applied text-size + font-weight utilities that can drift apart — see the tokens repo's build.mjs. Naming convention (2026-07-25): heading styles dropped the redundant "heading-" prefix (h1-h6 is already unambiguous on its own), and every weight-bearing suffix now uses the numeral (e.g. paragraph-medium-500, not paragraph-medium-medium) — "medium" meant two different things (a size tier and a font-weight) in the same name, which numerals resolve outright.

REPLACED 2026-10-05: the heading scale (display-large, display-small, h1-h6) is fully re-sourced from the Tahche Design System v2 Figma file's dedicated "Typography documentation set" page (Headers/Body/Other sub-pages, pulled via get_variable_defs on node 8333:18468) — this is a comprehensively re-documented spec, not an incremental correction, and it supersedes the prior single-weight heading values. Two structural changes: (1) headings now render in Montserrat (see typography.fontFamily.heading), not Inter — previously every typography token used the same Inter-based fontFamily.sans regardless of role; (2) every heading size now ships three confirmed weight variants (Medium/500, SemiBold/600, Bold/700), the same multi-weight pattern already used for paragraph-large/medium/small, rather than one hardcoded weight. The v2 file does not offer an Extrabold(800) option for any heading — the prior h1/h2/display-large weight of 800 was itself never confirmed by a real Figma variable (it was extrapolated from a foundation page whose own real-code counterpart, the Title component, actually rendered Bold/700); that 800 assumption is dropped, not carried forward. The bare h1/h2/h3/h4/h5/h6/display-large/display-small names are kept as deprecated aliases to one concrete weight variant each (the 700 that the old real-code evidence pointed to for h1/h2/display-large, and the already-confirmed h3/h4/h5/h6 weights carried forward unchanged) purely so existing class references — including {typography.h2} in this file's own component definitions — keep resolving; new work should pick a weight variant directly. Separately, every typography role now also carries a Mobile value (see each token's "mobile" field) sourced from the same Figma page — new in this pass, since the prior scale had no breakpoint-aware sizing at all. The Mobile field is additional, build-pipeline-only metadata (consumed by build.mjs for a max-width:767px override inside each composite class, 767px being one pixel under the ratified breakpoint.md = 768px cutoff); it is intentionally left out of DESIGN.md's frontmatter, whose component-sub-token schema is fixed by the real design.md lint CLI and only has room for the Web-default fontSize/fontWeight/lineHeight/letterSpacing (see generate-design-md.mjs). paragraph-medium, paragraph-small, and paragraph-xsmall also moved to the full numeral-suffix convention (paragraph-medium-400, etc.) in this pass, re-confirmed against the same Figma page; their old bare names are kept as deprecated aliases for the same reason as the headings above. overline split into overline-12 (the original, re-confirmed exactly as-is) and overline-14 (new size variant found on the same Figma page); "overline" is now a deprecated alias to overline-12.

sans.$description: The font actually rendered in all 5 apps today, applied via a global CSS override rather than Tailwind config. This token is what fixes that — register it as the Tailwind 'sans' default. Used for every body/paragraph/label/overline style; headings use typography.fontFamily.heading instead (see the 2026-10-05 note on the group description above).

heading.$description: NEW 2026-10-05, sourced from the Tahche Design System v2 Figma file's typography documentation page: every heading role (display-large, display-small, h1-h6) renders in Montserrat there, not Inter — Arial kept as the fallback, same chain shape as typography.fontFamily.sans. Per the user's own call on the Sept 2026 brand refresh (the refresh's color change was reverted as a flaw — see color.json — but its Montserrat/Arial typography direction was confirmed correct), this is treated as settled, not proposed.

Sitting 4px from h1 (solidly used in 4 of 5 apps) with no evidence anyone needs the distinction, this token is kept only so nothing that already references it breaks — new work should use h1 directly.
